text:
For running, the best open-ear options from these reviews are the **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** for overall sound, the **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** for a bone-conduction neckband, and the **Soundcore AeroFit 2** or **JLab Flex Open** if you want to spend less.

## Top picks

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**
- Runner's World calls these its overall pick. They aim sound at the ear canal, so less leaks out than from most open designs, and they have physical buttons that are easy to use while moving. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Tradeoffs: expensive, about 7 hours per charge, IPX4 water resistance, and one reviewer found them too quiet in heavy traffic. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Price: WIRED and Runner's World both list $199 on sale, down from $299.

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**
- Bone conduction keeps your ear canals fully open, and the air-conduction bass makes it fuller than older Shokz models. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- It's rated IP55 with about 12 hours of battery, and it has USB-C charging. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- Tradeoffs: clarity is weaker than the older OpenRun, and the neckband can catch on a high ponytail or a hood. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Price: Runner's World lists $180. WIRED lists $125 at some retailers, but that review is from 2024, so check current pricing.

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2**
- Open-ear hook design with LDAC on Android, IP55, about 10 hours per bud and 42 hours with the case. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- SoundGuys lists it as its best budget pick at $79.99, down from $99.99. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Dealectric reports code AFSC20 took $25.99 off at Soundcore's US store on Oct 22, 2026, for about $104. Its list price is $129.99, which doesn't match SoundGuys, so confirm the price at checkout. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- Buy link: [Soundcore AeroFit 2 at Soundcore's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link. Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Budget: JLab Flex Open Earbuds**
- Runner's World's budget pick. It's comfortable and loud enough for most settings, but the sound is weaker and it has touch controls only. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Price: the article lists $40 at Amazon but also says "$50," so check the current price.
- Cheaper alternative: the Soundpeats PearlClip Pro at $50 (WIRED). [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Longest battery: Shokz OpenDots 2**
- About 10 hours per charge, 40 hours with the case, and IP57 water and dust resistance. Runner's World also calls it its best for long runs. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Price: $200.

**Other options worth a look**
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' best for running. It has a strong bass response for an open design and an IP54 rating. Listed at $99 on sale. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)
- **Soundcore Aeroclip:** WIRED's runner-up, with good battery life and IP55 rating. Listed around $150. The Aeroclip 2 is newer. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Before you buy
- **Safety:** Open-ear designs let in traffic noise but don't block sound, so keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Sound:** Open designs usually sound less full than sealed earbuds. Bose and Shokz are the most-cited options for clarity and bass.
- **Fit:** Long hair, hats, and hoods can affect neckband and hook designs. Clip-ons avoid some of this.
- **Upcoming models:** Runner's World notes Bose plans a new open-ear model soon, so the Ultra Open may get a successor.
- **Prices:** These come from sources dated between September and October 2026. Prices vary, so check the retailer before buying. I don't have verified store links for the other products here, so search for the model name at your preferred retailer or use the review links above.
